purpose: Design options for user selection; fictional illustrative data, not implemented.
prompts:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high resolution wide comparison board for a real competitor ad research dashboard. Three equal-width alternative UI panels side by side on pure white, separated by generous gutters and fine grey rules. Each panel is one independent design option, not sections of one dashboard. Crisp Inter-like typography, charcoal text, restrained indigo accents and amber ONLY for financial assumptions. Professional Linear-like data UI, no shadows, no gradients, no decoration, no phone or laptop frames, no ad thumbnails. Large highly readable labels, clear chart geometry. Design-only previews, not live data. Prominent small footer across the board: "ILLUSTRATIVE DESIGN PREVIEW · Fictional data · Not competitor results". Landscape composition around 2400 by 1300. Each option has a large choice code, a short title, one short plain-language purpose sentence, and a detailed finished UI mockup below. Render all meaningful labels correctly. Do not add invented performance claims.
 Board heading: "SPENDING — choose how to handle uncertainty".
 Three options:
 S1 title "Evidence table". Purpose: "What spending evidence do we actually have?"
 Render a clean compact table with columns Ad / Amount / Basis. Rows: "Breakfast offer", "RM 1,000–2,000", "Impressions × assumed CPM"; "Customer story", "Unknown", "No delivery evidence"; "Weekend bundle", "Unknown", "No delivery evidence". These are illustrative source-based cases. Below table a small light amber note: "Estimates need delivery evidence. Age alone cannot reveal spend." Small text link "Add source evidence". This is the evidence-first recommended option, show small "Recommended" label.
 S2 title "Budget sensitivity". Purpose: "What would different budgets cost?"
 A 3 by 3 matrix, column headers "RM 100/day", "RM 200/day", "RM 300/day"; row headers "7 days", "14 days", "30 days". Correct cells 700 1400 2100; 1400 2800 4200; 3000 6000 9000. Amounts in MYR. Selected cell 14 days and RM200/day = "RM 2,800" with quiet amber outline. Caption "Hypothetical budget × days. Not their actual spend." No timeline or revenue projections.
 S3 title "Estimate calculator". Purpose: "Which input produces this range?"
 A polished two-input calculator: "Reported impressions" = "100,000"; "Assumed CPM" = "RM 10–20". Simple equation row "100,000 ÷ 1,000 × RM 10–20". Result "RM 1,000–2,000" in large clear type. Caption "Source-backed delivery + your price assumption". Outline uncertainty interval with two labeled endpoints, not a growth curve. Include small field "Evidence source" = "Illustrative report".

 Board heading: "AD AGE — choose the comparison".
 Use exactly these fictional linked ad titles and calendar ages everywhere: "Breakfast offer" 28 days; "Customer story" 8 days; "Weekend bundle" 3 days; "Product demo" 3 days.
 A1 title "Ranked ad table". Purpose: "Which ads have the earliest starts?" Small "Recommended" label. Clean table columns Rank / Ad / Age / Last check. Rows ranks1,2,3,3 and the four titles above with ages28d8d3d3d. Last check status Active, Active, Active, Unknown respectively, in quiet text. Use underlined indigo ad titles and small external-link icons. Subtle in-cell age mini-bars, optional but values dominant. Footer "Calendar age is not paid runtime."
 A2 title "Age dot plot". Purpose: "How far apart are the ad ages?"
 Four linked titles on left, clean horizontal numeric axis from0 to30 days with ticks0,10,20,30. One indigo dot each at28,8,3,3 with exact values next to dots. Sparse light vertical guide lines. No solid duration bars, no performance badges, no median or score invented. Footer "Older does not necessarily mean better."
 A3 title "Observation timeline". Purpose: "What did we actually observe?"
 Two linked ad rows. Date axis1Sept,10Sept,20Sept,30Sept. Breakfast offer has hollow source-start diamond at2Sept, solid observed dots at9Sept and30Sept; Customer story source-start diamond22Sept and one observed dot30Sept. Dotted connectors only, no filled continuous-running bars. Legend "◇ Source start", "● Saved check", "Dotted interval: delivery unknown". Small bottom note "Requires dated snapshots. This is an evidence timeline."

 Board heading: "LAUNCH ACTIVITY — choose what changes you want to notice".
 All options show the same fictional saved starts: 7 September 2026 one ad "Breakfast offer"; 27 September 2026 one ad "Customer story"; 1 October 2026 three ads "Weekend bundle", "Product demo", "Free shipping". Window7Sept–4Oct. Numbers describe saved collection only.
 L1 title "Launch feed". Purpose: "What appeared since my last review?" Small "Recommended" label. Compact chronological agenda grouped newest first: "1 Oct · 3 new starts" with three indigo linked ad titles; "27 Sept · 1 start" with Customer story; "7 Sept · 1 start" with Breakfast offer. Simple date gutter and fine separators, no huge blank calendar, no thumbnail. Small filter buttons "All" and "Since last review" as design affordances. Footer "Source start dates from saved ads."
 L2 title "Compact calendar". Purpose: "On which dates did ads start?"
 Two SMALL side by side monthly calendar grids September2026 and October2026 inside the panel, rather than a huge month occupying the whole page. Correct Monday-based calendar: September1 is Tuesday, October1 is Thursday. Highlight Sep7 with badge1, Sep27 badge1, Oct1 badge3. Only selected dates7Sept–4Oct emphasized. Selected Oct1. Beneath calendars show "1 Oct · 3 starts" and the three linked titles. Other dates neutral. Footer "An empty cell means no saved starts."
 L3 title "Weekly launch rhythm". Purpose: "Were starts clustered or spread out?"
 A clear vertical column chart with four week-start labels "7 Sep", "14 Sep", "21 Sep", "28 Sep" and counts1,0,1,3 respectively. Y axis0,1,2,3. Bars restrained indigo, exact count labels above all four categories, zero shown on baseline. Below chart selected summary "28 Sep–4 Oct: 3 saved starts" and three linked ad titles. Footer "Counts are not the advertiser’s complete activity."
